title: Merged Companies, Shared Bank Account
scenario_text: Grimsby Industrial's cash-application team is matching an incoming wire to open invoices. On 2024-05-02 a wire of $612,400 arrives from originating account routing 026009593 / account ending 7788, remitter name "Atlas Cutting Tools." The remittance advice references three invoice numbers. In NetSuite, Grimsby has two customer records: "Atlas Cutting Tools, Inc." (customer C-2201, EIN 04-3320119, open A/R $410,000) and "Redline Machining Co." (customer C-2890, EIN 26-1188742, open A/R $202,400). The three referenced invoices split across both records: two invoices totaling $410,000 belong to Atlas (C-2201) and one invoice of $202,400 belongs to Redline (C-2890). The cash-app clerk is confused because the wire came from an "Atlas" account but references a Redline invoice. Research reveals: on 2024-01-15, Atlas Cutting Tools, Inc. acquired Redline Machining Co. in an asset+entity acquisition; Redline became a wholly-owned subsidiary but retains its own EIN and continues to be invoiced as a separate customer under its existing contract. A treasury consolidation memo (emailed from treasury@atlasct.com) states that post-acquisition, "all group disbursements, including Redline's payables, now run through the Atlas master operating account ending 7788." Both customers' contracts remain separate in Ironclad; only the paying bank account was consolidated.
question: How much of the $612,400 wire should be applied to the Redline Machining (C-2890) customer record?
